title: The 4 Best Adjustable Dumbbells Under $400
metaDescription: Our 4 picks for adjustable dumbbells under $400, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at adjustable dumbbells under $400 using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: PowerBlock Elite EXP Stage 1 Adjustable Dumbbells, 5-50 lb (Pair)
products.blurb: Key specs: 5 to 50 lb per hand, expandable to 90 lb, Pin-selector weight system, Typically around $379.
strengths: Best mechanism-to-price ratio of the premium tier options under this ceiling
Genuine expansion path to 90 lb per hand if needed later
Compact footprint on top of a strong feature set
limitations: Costs more than Core Home Fitness for a similar 50 lb ceiling
Full expansion later adds real additional cost
features: 5 to 50 lb per hand, expandable to 90 lb

products.name: Core Home Fitness Adjustable Dumbbell Set & Stand
products.blurb: Key specs: 5 to 50 lb per hand, TwistLock one-hand cradle adjustment, Typically around $299.
strengths: Lowest price of the mid-to-premium mechanism options in this list
Simple, fast TwistLock system with minimal learning curve
limitations: 50 lb ceiling is the lowest of the mechanism-based picks here
Smaller install base and shorter track record than PowerBlock

products.name: Amazon Basics Adjustable Dumbbell Hand Weight Set, 38 lb with Case
products.blurb: Key specs: 38 lb total across two handles, Spin-lock collars, Typically $60 to $90.
strengths: Genuinely functional for beginner to early-intermediate training
Case-based storage needs no floor space for a stand
limitations: Slowest adjustment method compared to the mechanism-based picks above
19 lb max per hand caps long-term progression

products.name: Amazon Basics 40-Pound Adjustable Weight Set with Case
products.blurb: Key specs: 40 lb total plate and collar set, Threaded collars, Typically $70 to $90.
strengths: Similar low price to the 38 lb set with slightly more total weight
No mechanism to jam or maintain, just threaded collars
limitations: Threaded collars are slower to adjust than spin-lock or dial systems
Low total weight limits it to light training
features: 40 lb total plate and collar set

howWeChose: Picks are based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. We don't claim our own testing.
We do not list prices or star ratings because they change. Check Amazon for current details.
